answer: Like timber graded before it bears load, an agent must lock a refundable stake bond tied to one hardware attestation before it can transact; clones share the same bond, so growing a grove of fake identities multiplies cost instead of multiplying votes. A basalt-hard rule slashes the bond and revokes the attestation when two identities sign conflicting claims, and peers only trust attestations countersigned by identities with settled history, so a sybil grove cannot buy reputation cheaply.
